content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Durham

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's official eligibility criteria—typically a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-leadership experience, or a high school diploma plus five years. Verify your qualifications before enrolling to ensure you'll meet application requirements.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Attend all sessions synchronously from anywhere, interact with active certified practitioners, and build mastery of the PMBOK Guide framework. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement for PMP eligibility.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, apply directly to PMI through their official portal. Document your project-management experience, upload proof of your 35 contact hours, and pay the PMI examination fee. PMI will review and approve your application before you schedule your exam date.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, including practice exams and study materials, to reinforce your knowledge. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner. Sit for the computer-based PMP exam and demonstrate your mastery of project-management principles and practices.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) every three years to renew your PMP. Pursue training, volunteer leadership roles, and professional activities across PMI's learning categories. Granite PM Academy offers continuing-education opportunities to keep your credential active and your skills current.

fq_items.question: Do I need to travel to {city} for this training?
fq_items.answer: No. All of our PMP training is delivered live-virtual via video conference, so {city} professionals attend from wherever they work. No commuting or hotel required.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI requires either a four-year degree with 36 months of project leadership experience, or a high school diploma with 60 months of experience. All applicants need 35 contact hours of PM education — our course satisfies this requirement.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

fq_items.question: Is PMP certification worth pursuing for Durham project managers?
fq_items.answer: Yes, particularly if you work in healthcare, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, or technology—Durham's dominant sectors. Employers like Duke University Health System, IQVIA, and GSK frequently prefer or require PMP credentials for advancement into senior project and program management roles. Certified professionals typically command measurably higher compensation than non-certified peers, making the investment strategically sound for long-term career growth in the Research Triangle Park job market.

fq_items.question: Do Durham's major employers prefer PMP or CAPM certification?
fq_items.answer: Both are valued, but context matters. Large organizations such as Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina, Biogen, and Duke University actively seek PMP-certified project managers for complex initiatives. CAPM® appeals to early-career professionals and those transitioning into project management. In Durham's competitive healthcare and life sciences sectors, PMP certification is often listed as preferred or required; CAPM® serves as a credible entry point if you don't yet meet PMP eligibility requirements.

This flexibility is especially valuable if you work for major Durham employers with distributed teams or flexible work arrangements. You'll participate in real-time interactive sessions without geographic constraints, allowing you to balance training around your current project demands.

fq_items.question: How does Durham's job market affect PMP certification timing?
fq_items.answer: Durham's concentrated demand from healthcare, pharmaceutical, and technology employers means open project management roles often appear year-round, but hiring peaks align with budget cycles in spring and fall. If you're actively job-searching or targeting a promotion, pursuing certification before peak hiring seasons strengthens your candidacy. If you're employed and stable, timing your certification around slower work periods allows focused study without overwhelming your current responsibilities.
